content.text: {"narrative":[{"claim":"India faced a challenge in that fragmented definitions, reporting formats and data systems had made it difficult to measure progress consistently and spotlight inequalities.","cites":["risk:3"]},{"claim":"The Government of India launched the Swachh Bharat (Clean India) Mission in 2014, and the mission reached nearly every corner of the country by 2024.","cites":["fact:01a126b0-ed8a-71ce-8683-1ec079f39bba","kpi:38"]},{"claim":"Toilets constructed under the Swachh Bharat Mission were 110 million, and the Government of India's investment in water and sanitation was over $120 billion.","cites":["kpi:32","kpi:31"]},{"claim":"India reached 580 million people with improved drinking water and 550 million people with basic sanitation in the last 10 years.","cites":["kpi:29","kpi:28"]},{"claim":"In 2024, 59.3 million people in India accessed safely managed water and 17.9 million people accessed safely managed sanitation.","cites":["kpi:36","kpi:35"]},{"claim":"India launched the Jal Jeevan (Water is Life) Mission to achieve universal access to safe and adequate drinking water.","cites":["fact:01a126b0-ed8b-72d5-a947-4e59d98400da"]}]}
